title: namespace-gpu-pool-and-cross-account-iam-state-schema-v2
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Introduce tenant-scoped GPU nodepool module and a reusable cross-account IAM bindings module; add state schema v2 and a tfstate migrator helper. Upgrade notes included — operators must run migrator before applying new modules. No runtime behavior changes expected but terraform var names changed for tenant scoping.
description:
Motivation: Private deployments have accumulated ad-hoc GPU nodepool and IAM wiring across clusters. This PR factorizes GPU nodepool definitions into a tenant-scoped module (gpu_nodepool/namespace) and adds a composable cross-account IAM bindings module that centralizes principals for KMS/HSM and bastion access. It also formalizes a state layout (state_schema_version = "v2") to make per-environment, per-cluster, per-tenant state prefixes explicit and provides a small tfstate-migrator helper to move state without manual terraform state mv invocations.

Scope: single PR touching Terraform modules only (no application code). Changes target private deployment workflows used by the installer and by on-prem operator teams. The change set includes module API changes, docs, examples, and an opinionated migrator script to ease rollout.

Checklist:
- [x] Factorize gpu_nodepool into modules/gpu-nodepool/tenant_namespace (variables: tenant_id, env, cluster, gpu_profile)
- [x] Introduce modules/iam/cross-account-bindings with configurable principals and binding types (kms, hsm, bastion, service-account)
- [x] Add state schema variable state_schema_version and backend_prefix helper (default: v2)
- [x] Provide scripts/tfstate-migrator (Go binary) and state/migrations/README.md with migration plan
- [x] Update examples/private-deploy/* and add example for tenant layout
- [x] Run unit/integration terraform fmt/lint and a gated e2e that provisions a tiny private cluster in our test account

Compatibility and upgrade path:
- This is backwards-compatible at runtime but will require operators to run the migrator when switching to state_schema_version=v2. The migrator supports a dry-run mode and will generate the required terraform state mv commands for manual review.
- Variable rename notes: previous top-level gpu_pool_name becomes scoped as tenant_gpu_pool_name; mappings updated in examples. A short conversion table is in docs/upgrade-notes.md.

Migration steps (operator-facing):
1) Checkout branch and run make migrator-build to produce scripts/tfstate-migrator
2) ./tfstate-migrator --from-prefix="envs/old-layout" --to-prefix="envs/v2/clusterX/tenantY" --dry-run > planned-moves.txt
3) Review planned-moves.txt, then re-run without --dry-run to apply (or apply individual terraform state mv commands)
4) Update terraform backend config to set state_schema_version = "v2" and apply module changes

Testing and validation:
- Added unit tests that validate module variable schemas and local values (tests/terraform-unit)
- CI pipeline: terraform fmt -> tflint -> terraform init/validate -> gated e2e that runs the migrator in dry-run mode and creates a short-lived test instance (tests/e2e/private-cluster-alloc.yaml)

Rollout considerations:
- Staged rollout recommended: pick one non-production environment, run migrator, validate state, then proceed to prod clusters.
- The cross-account IAM bindings module intentionally separates the target principal list from binding creation to avoid accidental privilege escalation; reviewers should validate principal lists before apply.

Related work: ENG-5121 (tenant isolation for GPU pools), ENG-5248 (state hygiene and tfstate tooling).

Notes: This PR intentionally does not change RBAC policies beyond what's necessary for binding creation. A follow-up will land a Helm tweak in the private-installer to consume tenant-scoped names from the new module outputs.
